title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is axiomatizing the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}, meaning the boundary of the Deligne–Mumford compactification. This boundary is a normal crossings divisor (in the orbifold/stack sense). The axiomatization is phrased only through the normalized strata and their combinatorics.

The data, set up on the previous page:
- D_d is the normalization of the locus of points of multiplicity ≥ d. It parametrizes a point together with an unordered choice of d local branches. D_0 = X is the ambient space.
- D_d^! → D_d is the S_d-torsor of orderings of those d branches.
- D_{d,d'} = D_d^! ×^{S_d} D_{d'}(I_d) is the finite étale cover of degree C(d,d') that chooses d' of the d branches. One has D_{d,0} ≅ D_{d,d} ≅ D_d, and D_{d,1} is the d-sheeted 'branch' cover.
- The 'but' (target) maps b: D_{d,d'} → D_{d'} forget the non-chosen branches. A point lying on d' chosen branches is a point of the normalized d'-fold stratum.
- Compatibility (175): the pullback along b of the S_{d'}-torsor D_{d'}^! is the tautological torsor of orderings of the chosen d' branches.
- D_{d,d',d''} = D_{d,d'} ×_{D_{d'}} D_{d',d''}, which (176) identifies with nested choices d'' ⊂ d' ⊂ d.

This page adds the axiom (177). In the square, D_{d,d',d''} goes to D_{d',d''} by projection and then to D_{d''} by 'but'. Alternatively, D_{d,d',d''} goes to D_{d,d''} by the tautological map (composite of the nested choices) and then to D_{d''} by 'but'. The two composites must agree. This is the associativity/transitivity of the 'restriction to sub-branch-sets' maps.

In modern terms, the data is equivalent to a functor S ↦ D^!_S from the opposite of the category of finite sets and injections (FI^op) to spaces, with D_d = D^!_{[d]}/S_d. The axiom (177) is functoriality for composable injections. In other words, it is a symmetric semi-simplicial (symmetric Δ-) object built from the normalized boundary strata.

Remarks on the page:
(i) The axiomatics makes sense in any site, since principal coverings make sense there. One needs only that locally constant (integer-valued) functions decompose objects into disjoint sums.
(ii) One need not separately give the 'function' (the multiplicity/degree grading). It is contained in condition c), which implies a) and b).

Grothendieck then begins to link this axiomatics with the earlier notion of 'revêtements maximaux'. He imposes an ad hoc hypothesis on the maps D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}, noting that D_{d,d'} → D_d is finite étale. The next page specifies the hypothesis: these maps are local immersions (of smooth analytic spaces, possibly relative). It reduces this to D_d → D_0 = X being local immersions, and in the smooth case reinterprets it as a 'local normal crossings' condition meaningful in sites.

Purpose: to describe the tubular/boundary structure of M_{g,ν}, and of normal crossings divisors in general, intrinsically and site-theoretically. This is presumably meant to feed the description of the fundamental groupoid 'at infinity'.
errors: No substantive mathematical error. Axiom (177) is exactly the needed transitivity condition.

Remark (ii), that condition c) implies a) and b), is stated loosely. Strictly, the grading by d is recovered only once one has the decomposition by locally constant functions plus the torsor data. This is a matter of formulation, not a mistake.
The 'local immersion' hypothesis, introduced on the next page, is the correct normal-crossings condition only in the smooth (or relatively smooth) setting, which Grothendieck himself notes.

ideas.what: Encoding a normal crossings divisor by its normalized multiplicity strata D_d, the S_d-torsors of branch orderings, and restriction maps D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}, with transitivity axiom (177)
ideas.modern_name: FI^op-diagram / symmetric semi-simplicial space of boundary strata (the stratification underlying the boundary or dual complex); cf. Deligne's D^{(p)} with orientation torsors in mixed Hodge theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II, 1971) for the normalized strata with sign/orientation local systems. Chan–Galatius–Payne (2018–2021) for symmetric Δ-complexes as boundary complexes of M_{g,n}. Kato/Illusie-style log geometry for intrinsic local descriptions.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower informally; this axiomatics is not there in this form as far as I know.

ideas.what: Observation that the axiomatics makes sense in any site where locally constant functions decompose objects into disjoint sums
ideas.modern_name: Topos-theoretic/stacky formulation of normal crossings structures (e.g. in log stacks or Artin fans)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not specifically credited; implicit in later log-geometry and stack-theoretic treatments (Olsson, Abramovich–Chen–Marcus–Wise).

ideas.what: Hypothesis that the maps D_{d,d'} → D_{d'} (equivalently D_d → X) are local immersions, recovering the 'maximal coverings' picture
ideas.modern_name: Normalization of a normal crossings divisor as an immersion; 'normal crossings' as a local condition

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the boundary structure of M_{g,ν} as torsor-twisted, functorial data indexed by choices of sub-branch-sets, i.e. an FI^op / symmetric Δ-object, and stresses that it makes sense in an arbitrary site. This anticipates the symmetric Δ-complex viewpoint later used for boundary complexes of M_{g,n} (Chan–Galatius–Payne), but here at the level of spaces/stacks rather than just the combinatorial dual complex.
missed.quote: L'axiomatique précédente a un sens dans n'importe quel site ... où on suppose que les fonctions localement constantes définissent une décomposition en sommes disjointes d'un objet.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Supports historical credit for an intrinsic, site-theoretic axiomatics of normal crossings boundaries in the moduli-space context. It is a modest anticipation; the underlying mathematics is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but essentially routine axiomatization of normalized strata of a normal crossings divisor with branch-ordering torsors. The site-level generality and the implicit FI^op structure are mildly interesting historically but not mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: 'qu'on doit [?]' is probably 'qu'on a' (i.e. 'il faut demander de plus qu'on a commutativité').
'fonctions lieux [?] constantes' should read 'fonctions localement constantes'.
'Il ne s'agit [?] pas en fait de se donner la fonction' is likely 'Il n'y a pas lieu en fait de se donner la fonction (degré)'.
'faire des hypothèses' is struck and replaced by 'une hypothèse ad hoc'.
The parenthetical is likely '(NB D_{d,d'} → D_d est un revêtement fini étale ...)'.
'en sommes disjointes' should read 'en sommes disjointes d'un objet'.
